I tell them I was born atheist and was never indoctrinated to believe that anything supernatural is real.

I usually answer, "Of course."

This answer often results in a conversion attempt, because usually the one asking is "a person of faith", and you can't reason a person out of a position they didn't reason themselves into. Push comes to shove, I try to explain the difference between a theory (e.g. the Earth is about 4.6 billion years old) and how one goes about supporting a theory (e.g. the scientific method). Atheism isn't a belief any more than refutation of the Easter Bunny is a belief, nor is it the belief in No-God; it is instead the unwillingness to believe in unsubstantiated claims. Atheism is the inevitable consequence of requiring a rational explanation for all things.

At about this time, the person I'm talking with either looks on me with pity, starts to explain how I'm wrong using passages from their spell book, or gets angry and assures me I'm going to regret my blasphemy for all eternity -- or some combination of the three. The Greek voters have learned to vote welfare for themselves, sending the country into an economic death spiral.

Each nation that has breached the 50 percent barrier in public reliance is also showing poor growth with numerous nations coming dangerously close to the majority in some form of reliance on redistribution for earnings.
